content:
We're about to push the next Zombie Match 3D build (the one that ships as "Puzzles vs Zombies") to the App Store and Google Play, and I'm the one who has to make the go or no-go call on it. Before I sign off I want a real readiness check done against our actual release process, not just everyone telling me it looks fine. Please work through our Release Checklist and Store Submission page and treat it as the gate. Go through every item on it, both the Build and QA section and the Store metadata and compliance section, and every incident row in the Lessons from incidents table. For each one I don't want a tick, I want the real evidence for the build we're submitting and a clear read on whether it's actually satisfied. That means chasing down the engineering tickets behind each hardened item, whatever QA has actually said about this build, and the open bugs people are still threading in our submission-blockers channel. Keep in mind the two things that have bitten us before: QA sign-off is a hard gate, so no sign-off means it is not shippable, and the update path has to be checked from both of the last two shipped versions, not just a clean install, because a fresh-install-only pass does not clear this gate.

What I need out of this is a written go/no-go readiness report I can circulate. Lay it out item by item the way the checklist is ordered, and for each item give me a plain status of PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NEEDS-INFO along with the specific evidence you based it on, whether that was a ticket, a QA note or a thread. Close it with one overall call, GO or NO-GO, and if it's a no-go put the blockers that are stopping us right at the top. For anything that lands as FAIL or BLOCKED, make sure it's genuinely tracked: if there's already an engineering ticket, update it so it clearly reads as blocking this submission, and if there honestly isn't one, open one that captures the problem, the platform and version affected, and why it blocks the release. Then drop a short summary of the decision into the submission-blockers channel so the team sees it in the right place, and email the founders along with the QA and engineering leads so leadership has the call and the blocking items in writing before anything gets submitted. One thing to be clear on: do not submit the build or touch anything in the store consoles yourself. I make the final submission call, and this is the readiness pass that feeds into it. Ground everything in what's actually in our systems, and if an item genuinely can't be verified from anything we have, mark it NEEDS-INFO and tell me what's missing rather than assuming it's fine. I'd like this before end of day.
I will search Confluence for the "Release Checklist and Store Submission" page to locate our release gate criteria and
lessons from incidents.
I will search Confluence and Google Drive
for release checklist documents.

First-line playbook for the four player-facing issues that drive the bulk of our inbound. It lets anyone covering the queue triage, reply, and escalate consistently. Scope is the live titles: Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes"), Zombie Match 3D ("Puzzles vs Zombies" in stores) and Combo Fighter. When a symptom matches a known incident, say so plainly and give a real ETA rather than a canned apology.

Always capture platform + store version + device model and, where the player can find it, their in-game user id (Settings → About → tap the build number). Most escalations stall because the ticket is missing one of these.

Triage table

Match the reported symptom to the row, apply the resolution, and only escalate if the resolution does not clear it.

SymptomLikely causeFirst-line resolutionEscalate to
Lives not regenerating / timer stuckJuly 2025 scheduler outage (event/lives loop stalled)Confirm the window; grant a lives top-up as goodwill; reassure that regeneration resumes once the scheduler is advancingBackend (Live-Ops scheduler)
Lost progression / account back at level 1June 2025 device-ID wipe (new device id, old save orphaned)Look up the old user id by email/receipt and re-link the current install (see below)Backend (account re-link)
Quests not appearing / empty slotsNov 2024 quest incident (population/reset regression)Force a session refresh; if slots stay empty, collect user id + timestamp and flagDesign + Backend (quests)
Frozen on splash at ~22%May 2025 font/asset download stallAsk them to switch networks (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), clear app cache, and reinstall; confirm it reaches gameplayClient / QA

Account re-link (June 2025 wipe)

A device-ID change orphaned some saves, dropping players to a fresh level-1 account while their real progression still exists under the previous id. Do not tell them the data is gone.

  • Ask for the account email and, ideally, a store receipt or order id.
  • Look up the old user id in the support console by that email; confirm the level/coin balance matches their description.
  • File a re-link request to Backend with both ids so the current install points at the old save.

Never issue a compensating grant before a re-link — you would be topping up the empty new account, not the recovered one, and the balances double up after the merge. Grants come after the save is restored.

Canned responses

Personalise the greeting, keep the facts. Do not promise fixes we have not shipped.

  • Lives stuck: "We had a scheduler issue that paused life regeneration for some players; it's being addressed and your lives will resume filling automatically. I've added a top-up in the meantime."
  • Lost progress: "Your progression isn't lost — a device change created a new profile. Send me the email on the account and I'll re-link it to your original save."
  • Missing quests: "Quests should repopulate after a fresh session. If they're still empty, reply with your user id and when you noticed and I'll escalate."
  • Stuck at 22%: "That's a loading stall on our end. Please switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, clear the app cache, and reinstall."

Known-issue notes arrive from QA before a build ships — see the QA Regression Runbook — and symptoms found during a submission are mirrored here via the Release Checklist & Store Submission.

It applies to Zombie Match 3D (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies"), Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes") and Combo Fighter. Do not submit a build until every box below is ticked and QA has signed off — the checklist exists because every item on it maps to a real incident that shipped.

Always test the UPDATE path from the last two shipped versions (N-1 and N-2), not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression wipe reproduced only when updating over a previously-shipped build; a clean install looked perfectly healthy. A fresh-install-only pass does not clear this gate.

Pre-submission checklist

Build & QA

  • Full manual regression is green on real iOS and Android hardware — see the QA Regression Runbook. QA sign-off is a hard gate.
  • Update path verified from N-1 and N-2: level, coins and unlocks survive the update; no save/progression loss.
  • Splash and loading screen watched all the way to gameplay on a throttled connection and with the app cache cleared — no stall (see incidents below).
  • Live quest config, if touched, has passed QA and a canary — nothing pushed straight to the live quest server (see the Quest System — Design & Incident Postmortem).

Store metadata & compliance

  • Version and build number bumped; release notes drafted for both stores.
  • Screenshots, age rating and data-safety / privacy declarations current.
  • IAP products and prices active in App Store Connect and Play Console before submission.
  • Analytics build tagged so installs attribute correctly (Singular).

Domino Delights is in maintenance mode — the current build is tracked under ENG-2366 (Jul 2025): IAP catalog refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, and the lives regeneration fix. Run the same update-path and store checks against it; maintenance does not mean unreviewed.

Lessons from incidents

Each row is a bug that reached players. Treat the corresponding checklist item as non-negotiable.

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Owned by QA (Vincent); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes"), Zombie Match 3D (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies") and Combo Fighter. Keep it to ~45 minutes per title; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 ZM3D progression wipe only reproduced when updating from a previously-shipped version — a clean install looked perfectly healthy. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 ZM3D froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets. Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory — N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 ZM3D)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe reproduced on update only
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account; confirm entitlements restore

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release — fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

ProgressionPlay 3 levels, force-quit, relaunchLevel and currency persist; no reset to level 1YesYesYes
EconomyEarn + spend coins, buy a boosterBalances reconcile; booster consumed onceYesYesn/a

AdsWatch a rewarded ad to completionReward granted once; no double-grant on retryYesYesn/a

Known-issue regression cases

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

Font-download stall. On a fresh device the dynamic font pack could fail to download, freezing the UI at ~22% of the tutorial. Regression: install on a wiped device with a throttled connection; confirm a fallback font renders and load continues.

Progression reset. A device-identifier change once wiped returning players back to level 1. Regression: migrate a save across a reinstall; confirm the cloud save rehydrates and no reset occurs.

Quest not resetting / not populating. A bad deploy left the daily quest board empty. Regression: roll the clock across a UTC day boundary; confirm quests repopulate and completion state resets.

Device lab

The minimum matrix is one recent + one old device per platform. We keep a small physical lab plus a cloud device farm for the long tail.

PlatformRecentOld / min-specTablet
iOScurrent-gen iPhone, latest OSiPhone SE-class, oldest supported OSiPad (one gen)
Androidcurrent-gen Samsung / Pixellow-RAM device, oldest supported OSone Android tablet

Sign-off

QA posts the completed matrix in #ops and links it from the release ticket. A build without a green matrix does not get submitted — no exceptions during the weekday release window, and never on a Friday.

Owner: Arthur Blake (Engineering) · Space: ENG · Related ticket: ENG-1892

Live quest configuration is player-facing on both iOS and Android. Never push quest changes straight to the live quest server. QA sign-off and a canary are now mandatory — see the Lessons & Follow-ups section below.

Design: How the Quest System Works

The quest system drives the daily engagement loop on Domino Delights (internal codename GoD). A single quest-config service owns the catalog of quest templates; clients pull the active set on session start and render the daily quest tray.

Quest lifecycle

  • Population — at the daily boundary the quest server selects a template set and materializes concrete quest instances (target, reward, progress counters) per player segment.
  • Reset — the previous day's quests are cleared and a fresh set is populated. Reset is anchored to the player's local midnight, computed server-side.
  • Progression — gameplay events (levels cleared, boosters used, ad views) increment the matching quest counters; completion grants the reward.

Quest types

TypeTriggerTypical reward
PlayLevels cleared in a sessionCoins
BoosterBoosters usedBoosters
AdsRewarded-ad views completedCoins / lives

Quest templates are shared with the Live-Ops Event Engine so seasonal events can layer bonus quests on top of the daily set.

Incident Postmortem — Daily Quests Not Populating (ENG-1892)

On November 15, 2024 daily quests stopped populating entirely on both iOS and Android, and failed to reset the following day. Impact spanned roughly 73 hours until the fix redeployed.

Timeline

Time (UTC)Event
2024-11-15 17:42Alert: daily quest tray empty on live builds; no quests populated on iOS or Android.
2024-11-15 18:20Confirmed reset also failing; scoped to the quest-config service, not the clients.
2024-11-16Traced to a newly added Ads-type quest template auto-deployed to the quest server.
2024-11-18 16:30Bad ad quest removed; auto-deploy of quest changes disabled.
2024-11-18 17:44Quest server redeployed; quests re-populated and reset normally. Incident resolved.

Root cause

A new Ads-type quest was auto-deployed to the quest server without any testing. The malformed template caused the population/reset routine to fail for the whole catalog, so the daily set was never materialized — hence empty trays and no reset.

Because population is all-or-nothing per run, a single bad template takes down every quest for every player. There is no per-template isolation today.

Fix

  • Removed the offending Ads-type quest template from the catalog.
  • Disabled auto-deploy of quest changes to the live quest server.
  • Redeployed; quests re-populated and reset resumed.

Lessons & Follow-ups

  • No auto-deploy to live quests without QA sign-off.
  • Add a canary: stage new quest templates to a small segment and verify population/reset before full rollout.
  • Fold quest pushes into the Release Checklist & Store Submission so nothing ships unreviewed.

It was pretty simple ", "channel": "C090N54TG79", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1754523087.472789"}, {"ts": "1754531119.912099", "type": "message", "text": "There is a strong correlation between low win rates and continuation at individual levels according to the regression analysis whether it’s an MF level or default level ", "channel": "C090N54TG79", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1754523087.472789"}, {"ts": "1754526678.876489", "type": "message", "text": "I dug into the CSV and measured *level-to-level continuation* as users[L+1] ÷ users[L] within each A/B group, then related that to *win rate* and *average level duration* per level.
*What the data says*
1. *Win rate matters more than duration, especially in the MF group.*
    ◦ In MF, win rate is a strong predictor of continuing to the next level even after controlling for level index and duration. A +10 pp increase in win rate predicts about *+2.7 pp higher continuation*. Duration is not statistically meaningful.
    ◦ In Default, neither win rate nor duration is strongly predictive after controlling for level, though There is a mild positive trend for duration.
2. *Same-level comparison (MF vs Default) points to win rate, not duration.*
    ◦ Regressing *Δ continuation (MF − Default)* on *Δ win rate* and *Δ duration* across levels shows a positive effect for *Δ win rate* and near-zero for *Δ duration*. In short, when MF has higher win rate than Default at the same level, MF also tends to have higher continuation; duration differences do not explain the gap.
3. *Quintile contrast for intuition.*
    ◦ MF: levels in the top win-rate quintile have *~7.1 pp* higher continuation than the bottom quintile. The analogous contrast for duration is *~1.0 pp*.
    ◦ Default: win-rate contrast *~4.1 pp*, duration *~1.6 pp*.
I put summary tables, the diff-in-diff regression, and two quick scatterplots in the workspace above so you can skim the patterns visually.
*Actionable takeaways*
• *Prioritize raising win rate on low-continuation levels*, particularly in MF. Early candidates where both continuation and win rate are under 90% include:
    ◦ *MF:* Levels *4* (win 0.76, cont 0.82), *8* (0.63, 0.84), *12* (0.69, 0.85), *9* (0.85, 0.88), *7* (0.79, 0.89).
• *Default:* Levels *9* (0.77, 0.85), *23* (0.81, 0.89).
    ◦  These are listed in the “Early-Level Opportunities” table above.
• *Tune difficulty, not session length, to lift level-to-level retention.*
•  Use the knobs you already control (symbol count, spawn rates, pity, extra tiles, etc.) to nudge win rate up where continuation dips. The MF variant appears *more sensitive to win rate*, so small difficulty fixes should have noticeable retention impact There.
• *Keep durations in a comfortable band rather than pushing them up.*
•  Across levels, *longer duration does not systematically improve continuation*. Aim for a smooth time-to-win profile, but do not expect longer stages to move retention.
*Notes and next steps*
• A few continuation values exceed 1.0. That happens when distinct user counts rise between adjacent levels (data grouping, late entries, or session stitching). It does not change the directional conclusions but is worth cleaning in the next pass.
• For causality, the ideal follow-up is *user-level* modeling: logistic regression or survival analysis with last outcome (win/loss), time on level, retries, boosts, and player fixed effects. That will tighten the estimate of how much a win on level L drives starting L+1.

{"ok": true, "messages": [{"ts": "1765166298.676749", "type": "message", "text": "<!here> I updated the canvas with a checklist of the polishes we need to do", "channel": "C09UHHN6PFZ", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1765166298.676749", "reply_count": 1, "reply_users_count": 1, "latest_reply": "1765169928.031219"}, {"ts": "1764793154.009679", "type": "message", "text": "Short answer: for a venture-backed US studio like Harmony Games, you should assume *somewhere in the 20k–80k USD range for legal + related professional fees*, with a realistic “plan for pain” budget around *50k*. I will break down why and how to Push it to the low end.
I am not your lawyer or accountant, so treat this as planning guidance and sanity check, not formal advice.

1. What drives the cost
Key factors that matter for Harmony Games specifically:
1. *Type of company and complexity*
    ◦ Delaware C-corp with investors and a real cap table.
    ◦ Multiple SAFEs / equity holders.
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements across countries.
    ◦ Multiple commercial contracts (publishers, ad networks, platforms, vendors).
2. More complexity pushes you away from “simple startup dissolution” pricing and into custom work.
3. *Where fees show up*
4.  You are not just paying for “file a dissolution form”:
    ◦ corporate / securities law work.
    ◦ Contract review and termination.
    ◦ Employment and IP issues.
    ◦ Tax and accounting cleanup.
    ◦ Possibly some board / investor process work (consents, releases, etc.).
5. *Your goal*
    ◦ If you want a “clean, defendable shutdown” that future investors and acquirers will not side-eye, you will spend more than the absolute bare minimum.
    ◦ If you are ok with more “duct tape,” you can cut costs, but you increase risk of something biting you later.
2. Rough fee ranges by category
These are order-of-magnitude numbers for a company like yours, using a mix of decent startup counsel + a scrappy accountant, not BigLaw overkill.
A. corporate dissolution & governance: *10k–30k*
Covers things like:
• Board and stockholder approvals.
• Formal dissolution with Delaware, plus any foreign registrations (e.g. NC, CA, WA).
• Handling investor rights, preference stack, and confirming There is no distribution or a small pro-rata distribution.
• Drafting or reviewing:
    ◦ Plan of liquidation / dissolution.
    ◦ Officer certificates.
    ◦ Releases and indemnities where needed.
If everything is organized and you work with current counsel efficiently, you might land around *10k–15k*. If lots of custom questions, messy history, or negotiations, *20k–30k*.
B. Contracts, IP, and “shutting the business off”: *5k–20k*
Includes:
• Reviewing and terminating:
    ◦ publishing deals (Boombit, CrazyGames, etc.).
    ◦ Platform agreements ([ORG_NAME_0308], IronSource, ad networks).
    ◦ Vendor and contractor agreements.
• Cleaning up IP:
    ◦ Making sure all game code and assets are properly assigned to the company, so There is no surprise claim later.
    ◦ Deciding what happens to IP: kept in the entity that will be dissolved, sold, or assigned to founders or a new entity.
• Dealing with licenses (engine, SDKs) and privacy / data issues.
If you have reasonably standard contracts and you are willing to send most termination notices yourself, lawyer time can be *5k–10k*. If There is negotiation, disputes, or an IP transfer / sale, *15k–20k+* is possible.
C. Employment, severance, and international wrinkles: *5k–20k*
You have:
• At least one US employee (WA).
• Contractors or employees in Turkey / Balkans / El Salvador, etc.
Items:
• Drafting or reviewing separation/severance agreements.
• Making sure state and country-specific rules are respected (notice, unused PTO, local labor rules).
• Confirming There are no outstanding claims or obvious liabilities.
If headcount is small and fairly aligned and you keep severance simple, legal review might be *5k–10k*. If you need local counsel in multiple countries or any disputes, *15k–20k+*.
D. Tax, accounting, and filings (non-legal): *5k–15k*
This is not legal fees but you have to budget it together:
• Final federal and state Tax returns.
• Sales tax / VAT cleanups if relevant.
• Final payroll / 1099s / T4s / foreign equivalents.
• Closing books, documenting treatment of remaining assets and liabilities.
A lean setup with a good startup CPA who already knows your books might be *5k–8k*. If There is multi-state, multi-country complexity and messy historical books, *10k–15k+*.
E. Contingency and “stuff you didn’t think of”: *5k–10k*
Even with good planning you will get:
• Extra questions from investors.
• A weird contract clause someone finds late.
• A platform or partner who needs a custom letter.
Having *5k–10k* in reserve avoids getting stuck mid-process.

3. Putting it together
For a harmonygames-like profile (Delaware C-corp, external investors, small global team, several commercial agreements, no massive litigation):
• *Very lean scenario, disciplined, everything clean:*
    ◦ Legal: 15k–25k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 5k–8k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k
    ◦ *Total: ~25k–38k*
• *More realistic “not perfect but not a mess” scenario:*
    ◦ Legal: 25k–45k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 8k–12k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k–10k
    ◦ *Total: ~38k–67k*
• *If things are messy or negotiated (IP sale, disputes, local counsel in multiple countries):*
    ◦ Legal: 40k–70k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 10k–15k
    ◦ Contingency: 10k
    ◦ *Total: ~60k–95k*
If you want a single planning number, I would assume *50k all-in* as a defensible budget, then work aggressively to drive it down.

4. How to Push toward the low end
If you decide to seriously plan for this, concrete things you can do now so fees do not explode:
1. *Organize everything:*
    ◦ Clean cap table and stock / SAFE docs in one folder.
• All major contracts in one spreadsheet with:
        ▪︎ Counterparty
        ▪︎ Term / termination clause
    ◦ Notice period
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements and any option grants clearly filed.
2. *Standardize the exit pattern:*
• Decide in advance:
        ▪︎ Severance formula, if any.
        ▪︎ End dates and communication plan.
    ◦ What happens to IP.
    ◦ Then ask counsel to just “paper this plan,” not design it from scratch.
3. *Have existing counsel give a scoped quote:*
• Ask for:
        ▪︎ A fixed or capped fee for core dissolution package.
    ◦ Hourly for “extras” like complex negotiations or IP sale.
    ◦ Get at least one alternative quote from a smaller startup firm.
4. *Do founder work where possible:*
    ◦ Draft first pass of partner termination emails.
    ◦ Fill out standard forms where allowed.
    ◦ Only loop counsel for review and the parts that carry legal risk.
5. What I would actually do in your shoes
If you are purely planning, not pulling the plug:
• Mentally earmark *50k* as “shutdown runway” in your long-range model.
• In the next quiet window, email current counsel something like:
    ◦ “If we needed to do an orderly dissolution with no contentious issues and minimal distributions, roughly what ballpark would you expect in fees, and what can we do now to make that lower?”
• Make sure your books and cap table are clean enough that you can actually execute a shutdown without a 3-month archaeology project.

What stays the same during an app transfer:
• *Bundle ID* (`com.calmplay.zombie`) — remains the same
• *App Store URL*
• *user reviews and ratings*
• *App history / versioning*
• *Existing installs and users*
What changes:
• The *App Store publisher name* (now shown as Harmony Games)
• The *developer account* managing the app
• Some internal IDs (used by App Store Connect or Google Play Console)
Regarding Singular:
Yes, if your *Singular setup keys off the app owner or organization*, you *may need to set this up as a new app* in Singular for data collection, attribution, or cost aggregation — just like you did for *Domino Adventures* and *Domino Delights* when those were handled under different orgs.
You’d just point it to the same bundle ID (`com.calmplay.zombie`), but under the new context/account.

{"id": "page_release_checklist", "space_id": "space_OPS", "parent_id": "page_ops_home", "title": "Release Checklist & Store Submission", "body": "

Owner: Vincent Parker (QA) · Space: OPS. This is the gate every Harmony Games title passes before we submit a build to the App Store or Google Play. It applies to Zombie Match 3D (store name \"Puzzles vs Zombies\"), Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \"Game of Dominoes\") and Combo Fighter. Do not submit a build until every box below is ticked and QA has signed off — the checklist exists because every item on it maps to a real incident that shipped.

Always test the UPDATE path from the last two shipped versions (N-1 and N-2), not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression wipe reproduced only when updating over a previously-shipped build; a clean install looked perfectly healthy. A fresh-install-only pass does not clear this gate.

Pre-submission checklist

Build & QA

  • Full manual regression is green on real iOS and Android hardware — see the QA Regression Runbook. QA sign-off is a hard gate.
  • Update path verified from N-1 and N-2: level, coins and unlocks survive the update; no save/progression loss.
  • Splash and loading screen watched all the way to gameplay on a throttled connection and with the app cache cleared — no stall (see incidents below).
  • Live quest config, if touched, has passed QA and a canary — nothing pushed straight to the live quest server (see the Quest System \u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem).

Store metadata & compliance

  • Version and build number bumped; release notes drafted for both stores.
  • Screenshots, age rating and data-safety / privacy declarations current.
  • IAP products and prices active in App Store Connect and Play Console before submission.
  • Analytics build tagged so installs attribute correctly (Singular).

Domino Delights is in maintenance mode — the current build is tracked under ENG-2366 (Jul 2025): IAP catalog refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, and the lives regeneration fix. Run the same update-path and store checks against it; maintenance does not mean unreviewed.

Lessons from incidents

Each row is a bug that reached players. Treat the corresponding checklist item as non-negotiable.

ENG-2343ZM3D global launch, May 15 2025Splash / loading screen resolution issue at launch.Verify splash and loading render correctly across device resolutions.
—Progression wipe, June 2025Player progression wiped on update; reproduced on the update path only, not fresh install.Test update from N-1 and N-2; confirm save/progression integrity.
ENG-2366Domino Delights maintenance, Jul 2025Maintenance build: IAP refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, lives fix.Run full store + update checks even on maintenance-mode builds.

When any check fails, block the release, file the bug with device / OS / source build, and do not ship until it is green.

Lost progression / account back at level 1June 2025 device-ID wipe (new device id, old save orphaned)Look up the old user id by email/receipt and re-link the current install (see below)Backend (account re-link)
Quests not appearing / empty slotsNov 2024 quest incident (population/reset regression)Force a session refresh; if slots stay empty, collect user id + timestamp and flagDesign + Backend (quests)
Frozen on splash at ~22%May 2025 font/asset download stallAsk them to switch networks (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), clear app cache, and reinstall; confirm it reaches gameplayClient / QA

Account re-link (June 2025 wipe)

A device-ID change orphaned some saves, dropping players to a fresh level-1 account while their real progression still exists under the previous id. Do not tell them the data is gone.

  • Ask for the account email and, ideally, a store receipt or order id.
  • Look up the old user id in the support console by that email; confirm the level/coin balance matches their description.
  • File a re-link request to Backend with both ids so the current install points at the old save.

Never issue a compensating grant before a re-link — you would be topping up the empty new account, not the recovered one, and the balances double up after the merge. Grants come after the save is restored.

Canned responses

Personalise the greeting, keep the facts. Do not promise fixes we have not shipped.

  • Lives stuck: "We had a scheduler issue that paused life regeneration for some players; it's being addressed and your lives will resume filling automatically. I've added a top-up in the meantime."
  • Lost progress: "Your progression isn't lost — a device change created a new profile. Send me the email on the account and I'll re-link it to your original save."
  • Missing quests: "Quests should repopulate after a fresh session. If they're still empty, reply with your user id and when you noticed and I'll escalate."
  • Stuck at 22%: "That's a loading stall on our end. Please switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, clear the app cache, and reinstall."

Known-issue notes arrive from QA before a build ships — see the QA Regression Runbook — and symptoms found during a submission are mirrored here via the Release Checklist & Store Submission.

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Owned by QA (Vincent); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes"), Zombie Match 3D (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies") and Combo Fighter. Keep it to ~45 minutes per title; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 ZM3D progression wipe only reproduced when updating from a previously-shipped version — a clean install looked perfectly healthy. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 ZM3D froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets. Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory — N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 ZM3D)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe reproduced on update only
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account; confirm entitlements restore

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release — fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

Known-issue regression cases

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

Font-download stall. On a fresh device the dynamic font pack could fail to download, freezing the UI at ~22% of the tutorial. Regression: install on a wiped device with a throttled connection; confirm a fallback font renders and load continues.

Progression reset. A device-identifier change once wiped returning players back to level 1. Regression: migrate a save across a reinstall; confirm the cloud save rehydrates and no reset occurs.

Quest not resetting / not populating. A bad deploy left the daily quest board empty. Regression: roll the clock across a UTC day boundary; confirm quests repopulate and completion state resets.

The minimum matrix is one recent + one old device per platform. We keep a small physical lab plus a cloud device farm for the long tail.

[{"id": "page_live_ops_engine", "space_id": "space_ENG", "parent_id": "page_eng_home", "title": "Live-Ops Event Engine", "body": "

The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D (\"Puzzles vs Zombies\" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content \u2014 Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode \u2014 and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12\u201326, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially \u2014 on the order of 30% across the outage \u2014 as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System \u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem.

Owner: Arthur Blake (Engineering) \u00b7 Space: ENG \u00b7 Related ticket: ENG-1892

Live quest configuration is player-facing on both iOS and Android. Never push quest changes straight to the live quest server. QA sign-off and a canary are now mandatory \u2014 see the Lessons & Follow-ups section below.

Design: How the Quest System Works

The quest system drives the daily engagement loop on Domino Delights (internal codename GoD). A single quest-config service owns the catalog of quest templates; clients pull the active set on session start and render the daily quest tray.

Quest lifecycle

  • Population \u2014 at the daily boundary the quest server selects a template set and materializes concrete quest instances (target, reward, progress counters) per player segment.
  • Reset \u2014 the previous day's quests are cleared and a fresh set is populated. Reset is anchored to the player's local midnight, computed server-side.
  • Progression \u2014 gameplay events (levels cleared, boosters used, ad views) increment the matching quest counters; completion grants the reward.

Quest types

TypeTriggerTypical reward
PlayLevels cleared in a sessionCoins
BoosterBoosters usedBoosters
AdsRewarded-ad views completedCoins / lives

Quest templates are shared with the Live-Ops Event Engine so seasonal events can layer bonus quests on top of the daily set.

Incident Postmortem \u2014 Daily Quests Not Populating (ENG-1892)

On November 15, 2024 daily quests stopped populating entirely on both iOS and Android, and failed to reset the following day. Impact spanned roughly 73 hours until the fix redeployed.

Timeline

Time (UTC)Event
2024-11-15 17:42Alert: daily quest tray empty on live builds; no quests populated on iOS or Android.
2024-11-15 18:20Confirmed reset also failing; scoped to the quest-config service, not the clients.
2024-11-16Traced to a newly added Ads-type quest template auto-deployed to the quest server.
2024-11-18 16:30Bad ad quest removed; auto-deploy of quest changes disabled.
2024-11-18 17:44Quest server redeployed; quests re-populated and reset normally. Incident resolved.

Root cause

A new Ads-type quest was auto-deployed to the quest server without any testing. The malformed template caused the population/reset routine to fail for the whole catalog, so the daily set was never materialized \u2014 hence empty trays and no reset.

Because population is all-or-nothing per run, a single bad template takes down every quest for every player. There is no per-template isolation today.

Fix

  • Removed the offending Ads-type quest template from the catalog.
  • Disabled auto-deploy of quest changes to the live quest server.
  • Redeployed; quests re-populated and reset resumed.

Lessons & Follow-ups

  • No auto-deploy to live quests without QA sign-off.
  • Add a canary: stage new quest templates to a small segment and verify population/reset before full rollout.
  • Fold quest pushes into the Release Checklist & Store Submission so nothing ships unreviewed.

### Core Gameplay
Match 3 identical objects triggers correct animation and throws to zombies
Killing all regular zombies completes the level
Killing boss zombie completes the level, even if regular zombies remain

Matching fewer than 3 does not trigger zombie damage
Level starts and ends properly without crashing
No soft-locks when all matchable objects are exhausted
Different object types trigger distinct visual/audio feedback
Boss hit and kill animations play correctly
### Boosts and Power-Ups
Boost button is tappable and triggers intended effect
Fast-match bonus throws items more quickly
Boss-targeting item exclusively damages boss
Using multiple boosts doesn't crash or bug the system
Boost usage shows visual feedback and is consumed properly
### UI / UX
Object tap, drag, and drop interactions are responsive
Pause, resume, restart functions operate correctly
Health bars for zombies and bosses update correctly
End-of-level UI appears consistently (success/failure)
HUD reflects real-time status of lives, moves, boosts
### Level Flow
Level begins from map screen correctly
Level completion popup appears
Level failure conditions trigger properly (moves/time out)
Retry, next level, and home buttons work as expected
Game state saved between sessions (e.g. retry level works)
### Packs & Upgrades
Pack opening animation and item rewards are displayed
Object inventory updates correctly after pack opens
Upgrade button is clickable only when enough materials exist
Upgrade improves stats (visible in UI and functional in play)
Duplicate objects are merged or stacked correctly in inventory
---
## 2. Edge Case Testing
### Gameplay Edge Cases
Matching 3 items when only 1 zombie remains (overkill behavior)
Using a boss-target item when no boss is present
Matching more than 3 identical objects (combo or error handling)
Attempting invalid match (e.g., rapid-tap glitch abuse)
Boost used in final second of level - is effect honored?
Level ends while object is mid-air - does game finalize properly?
### Progression and Upgrades
Opening a pack with max inventory space - is overflow handled?
Upgrading an already-maxed object - proper error or feedback
Internet lost during pack opening - graceful recovery?
Player skips tutorial - is core gameplay still understandable?
### Monetization
Purchase attempt without internet connection
Canceling mid-purchase - no item rewarded
Buying the same pack twice in a row - no duplication bugs
Receiving bonus pack from event, but pack cap reached
Purchase UI feedback is consistent across currencies (soft/hard)
Cross-platform purchase support (if applicable)
### UI/UX Edge Cases
Switching apps mid-level and returning - game state intact
Rotating screen (if supported) - UI remains consistent
Spamming object taps or boosts - system remains stable
Memory usage with long sessions or dozens of objects on screen
Language change mid-session - UI responds correctly
---
## 3. Persona-Based Scenario Testing
### Casual Player (Slow Progression, No Spending)
Can complete early levels without boosts or upgrades
Gets regular pack rewards from natural progression
Lives deplete on failure; soft-fail feedback encourages retry
Level difficulty gradually increases but remains fair
Onboarding tutorial teaches all core mechanics clearly
Ads appear after failure or level end but don't overwhelm
### Strategic Player (High Skill, Selective Spending)
Can clear levels through object prioritization and combos
Finds value in boss-targeting and fast-match mechanics
Upgrades objects from earned packs efficiently
Challenge levels or boss levels provide skill-based tests
Progression unlocks strategic layers like enemy types, object effects
### Payer / Whale (Frequent Buyer)
Can immediately purchase packs, boosts, lives
Progresses faster and accesses higher-level content
Boost stacking and usage remains balanced and not overpowered
UI confirms all transactions and feedback is instant
Exclusive content available but doesn't break balance
### Grinder (Long Play Sessions)
Multiple sessions without restart work smoothly
Game performance holds after 10+ levels without lag
No daily limits block grinding, but progression remains balanced
Performance degrades gracefully on low-end devices
Inventory and stats remain stable across extended gameplay
### Event-Driven Player
Event banners load and link properly
Event rewards contribute meaningfully to progress
Special event levels integrate with base mechanics
Timed events expire gracefully and give appropriate fallback content
Limited-time offers and countdowns are clear and functional

*RELEASE READINESS CALL: NO-GO for Zombie Match 3D v1.0.71 ("Puzzles vs Zombies")*

The pre-submission release readiness check for Zombie Match 3D v1.0.71 ("Puzzles vs Zombies") has returned **NO-GO**. Build 1.0.71 cannot be submitted to App Store Connect or Google Play Console at this time.

*Primary Submission Blockers:*
1. *QA Sign-Off Gate Unmet (ZOM-2439):* Full manual regression on real iOS and Android hardware has not been completed or signed off by QA Lead Vincent Parker.
2. *Unverified Update Path (ZOM-2440):* No N-1 and N-2 update path testing (from previous two shipped versions) has been conducted to ensure save/progression integrity.
3. *Active Progression & Sync Bugs (ZOM-667, ZOM-542 / PR #543):* Lives desync upon login/reinstall and Endless Mode score calculation regressions remain unresolved or pending QA validation.
4. *Live Quest Canary & Config Gate (ZOM-663, ZOM-641):* Quest configurations and level lists were modified without QA canary testing or staging validation (violating ENG-1892 process).
5. *Unverified Singular Analytics Tagging (ZOM-2438):* Install attribution and event tracking are unvalidated for 1.0.71.
6. *Incomplete Store Metadata & Catalog (ZOM-637):* Release notes for iOS/Android, screenshots, data safety declarations, and shop card-pack removals are incomplete.

Full detailed report circulated to leadership via email. Do NOT submit this build or alter store console state.

*URGENT: RELEASE READINESS REPORT - Zombie Match 3D v1.0.71 ("Puzzles vs Zombies")*

*OVERALL DECISION: NO-GO*

The readiness pass for Zombie Match 3D v1.0.71 ("Puzzles vs Zombies") is complete. The build is *NOT SHIPPABLE* and cannot be submitted to App Store Connect or Google Play Console.

*Primary Submission Blockers:*
1. *QA Sign-Off Gate Unmet [ZOM-2439]:* Full manual regression on real hardware has not been run or signed off by QA Lead Vincent Parker.
2. *Unverified Update Path [ZOM-2440]:* Save and progression integrity testing from N-1 and N-2 versions was not conducted.
3. *Active State & Progression Bugs [ZOM-667, ZOM-542 / PR #543]:* Lives desync on login/reinstall and Endless Mode score doubling for returning players remain unresolved or unvalidated.
4. *Unverified Live Quest Config [ZOM-663, ZOM-641]:* Quest configs were changed without passing QA sign-off or canary rollout.
5. *Unvalidated Singular Analytics [ZOM-2438]:* Install attribution tagging is unverified.
6. *Incomplete Store Metadata [ZOM-637]:* Store release notes, screenshots, data safety declarations, and shop card-pack removals are incomplete.

Full report is available in Google Docs ("RELEASE READINESS REPORT - Zombie Match 3D v1.0.71 (Puzzles vs Zombies) - NO GO").
All blocking items have been updated or created as high-priority Linear tickets under team_ZOM. Build submission is strictly halted until all items are resolved.

   * **Why It Blocks:** Per company release policy, QA sign-off is a strict hard gate with

zero exceptions.

   * **Problem:** Save and progression integrity testing when updating

from the last two shipped store versions (N-1 and N-2) has not been performed or documented.  
   * **Why It
Blocks:** Fresh-install testing alone does not clear this gate. Save/progression loss on update path has previously caused catastrophic player wipes

(June 2025 incident).

542 / PR #543:** Endless Mode score calculation doubles scores for returning players updating from prior versions.

QA staging verification or a canary rollout.  
   * **Why It Blocks:** Violates the Quest System process established

crashes and broken progression.

* **Problem:** Singular SDK tagging and event pipelines for build 1.0.71 have not been validated
